Which of the following statements about malware are TRUE?
I. A virus requires a user to execute or open a file to activate, whereas a worm spreads between computers without human interaction.
II. Fileless malware hides its code inside files that are concealed from the operating system, which is why anti-malware cannot scan it.
III. A rootkit embeds itself in the operating system and can make itself invisible to detection.

<button class=""l-check-btn"" onclick=""checkMCQ('q2','B','I and III are exact CED facts. II is false: fileless malware lives in RAM and abuses legitimate installed programs — it has no file for a signature scan to match, which is a different reason than hiding files.')"">Check Answer</button>
